PullRequest.Title: agentHost: refresh discovery after account entitlement changes
PullRequest.Body:

Agent Host can keep reporting an older Copilot entitlement after the workbench learns that the same account has gained access. For example, signing up for Copilot Free can leave successful requests labelled `no_access` until the host's independent discovery cache refreshes.

Forward an optional, account-scoped entitlement hint through the existing authentication path when the observed SKU changes, even if the credential stays the same. The host verifies the analytics identity against its own discovery and re-fetches using its own credential; it does not accept the client's SKU as authoritative.

Revalidation runs separately from credential acceptance and normal cached discovery, so a slow refresh does not hold up same-token authentication or revocation. Same-account connector credentials retain the originating account-session association, and superseded endpoint contexts cannot initiate the new lookup.

Add one account-discovery telemetry event per actual user-endpoint lookup so fresh endpoint responses can be distinguished from stale or superseded cache metadata. It records returned account/SKU metadata, HTTP tracing information, outcome, duration, and previous cache age, without introducing discovery snapshot IDs or adding fields to turn/tool/SDK response events.

Related: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10006.

To exercise the behavior, keep an Agent Host connected while refreshing the same account's entitlement after a plan change. Subsequent host telemetry should use the freshly discovered SKU without requiring token rotation or waiting for cache expiry. A different account's entitlement hint must not replace the host's metadata.

Live account/plan transitions have not been exercised locally.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed failure branch, cache read/write logic, and request call path are explicit: refresh starts only with a readable cached entry; the branch clears it on network/5xx/parse errors; `_getClientForToken` is awaited by all CAPI model operations and `_getEntryForToken` performs discovery when the value is absent. The exact network duration is environment-dependent, but the added critical-path request is deterministic after this trigger and coalesced to one request per token/host.
Findings.PerformanceResource: one additional `/copilot_internal/user` network request per affected token/host, plus client reconstruction
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost is one coalesced discovery round trip for each agent-host/token whose entitlement refresh fails, so it scales with active local/remote hosts and failed entitlement-change revalidations rather than with individual concurrent model calls.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked critical path and increased request latency from an avoidable network cache miss
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR, an entitlement change did not launch this background refresh or clear a valid host discovery entry, so subsequent model operations continued using the cached CAPI client until its normal refresh window. Existing ordinary refresh failures also retain an unexpired entry.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: A failed background entitlement revalidation now removes the still-valid per-token CAPI client/cache entry. The next models, responses, messages, utility completion, or telemetry-context lookup rebuilds the client through `/copilot_internal/user` before proceeding.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added non-authentication failure branch at src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/shared/copilotApiService.ts:968 assigns `request.skuCell.value = undefined` after an entitlement-triggered background refresh fails, even though `entry` was read from an unexpired cache value at line 938. `_getEntryForToken` then treats the next request as an initial miss and calls `_buildClientForToken`, while before this PR no entitlement refresh could evict that valid entry.
Findings.Title: Preserve the valid client after a failed background refresh
Findings.Impact: If entitlement revalidation encounters a transient network error, 5xx, or malformed response, the next chat/model or utility operation is delayed by an extra account-discovery round trip before its real request. If discovery is still unavailable, the user-facing operation fails after waiting on that extra boundary. This occurs once per affected token and host after each failed entitlement refresh; concurrent callers coalesce behind the same lookup.
Findings.Evidence: `refreshCopilotUser` obtains an unexpired `entry` via `_readCachedClient`, then on any non-401/403 failure clears `request.skuCell.value`. `_getEntryForToken` only returns immediately when that value exists; otherwise it awaits `_buildClientForToken`, whose changed code fetches `${getApiBaseUri()}/copilot_internal/user`. Public `models`, `responses`, `utilityChatCompletion`, and `_sendRequest` all await `_getClientForToken` before issuing their actual CAPI request. The existing ordinary-refresh failure path already preserves an unexpired `existing` entry, demonstrating the cache can remain usable across transient discovery failures.
Findings.Recommendation: On non-authentication refresh failures, retain the previous client until its normal expiry, as the ordinary refresh path does. If stale SKU telemetry must be suppressed, track that validity separately from the routing/client cache rather than converting the next model request into a discovery miss.

Scenarios.Scenario: A default-account entitlement change is forwarded to a connected local Agent Host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Authentication-session resolution and the authenticate RPC must complete for the workbench reconciliation, but `CopilotAgent.authenticate` deliberately launches entitlement discovery without awaiting it, so the new `/copilot_internal/user` refresh is off the same-token authentication critical path. Initial token authentication still awaits its existing discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward the same token plus entitlement metadata from the workbench to the Agent Host and fan it out to matching providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one new authenticate RPC per protected resource for each distinct account/tracking-ID/SKU tuple; repeated reconciliation with unchanged metadata is suppressed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The account-change listener already re-resolved authentication sessions, but same-token calls were suppressed by the token cache because entitlement was not part of its key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The RPC is part of account-change reconciliation, but the HTTP revalidation it starts is not awaited by the Copilot provider.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET `/copilot_internal/user` to revalidate CAPI endpoint and account metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for a changed matching entitlement per token/host after coalescing; no request for another account, equal SKU, absent/expired entry, or repeated identical hint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Entitlement changes did not trigger discovery before cache expiry or another ordinary client lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the same-token authentication critical path because `CopilotAgent.authenticate` does not await `refreshCopilotUser`.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Construct and enqueue a bounded account-discovery telemetry event after an actual lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small event per actual discovery request, including existing initial/cache-refresh requests and new entitlement requests; none on cache hits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Discovery requests emitted no dedicated telemetry event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Called synchronously at discovery settlement but carries fixed-size scalar metadata; no scaling payload or reportable critical-path cost was established.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of protected resources and connected hosts for the changed default account; effective network cardinality is one per matching token/host, not per agent or concurrent caller.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Agents and protected resources are traversed sequentially in the workbench. The host fans one resource authentication to matching providers with `Promise.allSettled`; entitlement HTTP refreshes are coalesced per token/request object. A newer changed hint waits behind an in-flight workbench authentication for the same resource key.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The workbench authentication cache now keys on token, account, tracking ID, and SKU, so unchanged hints are warm-cache hits and send no RPC; one changed hint causes a new authenticate RPC. In the host, refresh occurs only when an unexpired discovery entry has the same tracking ID and a different SKU. `_entitlementRefreshes` coalesces concurrent refreshes for that per-token request object.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event wiring, credential-key invalidation, provider IPC, host cache checks, non-awaited scheduling, and per-token coalescing are all directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Plan changes are infrequent and authentication-provider latency varies, so aggregate volume is uncertain; the one-RPC/one-HTTP changed mechanism is nevertheless explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the added refresh is the intended bounded work, is deduplicated, and is kept off same-token authentication progress.

Scenarios.Scenario: The same entitlement change is propagated to multiple remote Agent Host connections
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The default-account listener starts authentication for every connected remote host without awaiting the collection. Within each connection, session resolution and protected resources are sequential; each host's entitlement HTTP lookup remains off its authenticate response path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authenticate each connected remote host with the changed entitlement metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC per affected protected resource per connected remote host after each connection's token-cache deduplication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The listener already reconciled every connection, but same-token authenticate RPCs were suppressed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs asynchronously from the account-change event and does not serialize all remote connections.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Each remote Agent Host independently fetches `/copilot_internal/user` with its own credential.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one concurrent lookup per affected token per host; aggregate burst scales with the number of connected remote hosts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No entitlement-triggered lookup occurred on those hosts until normal cache refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off each same-token authenticate call's critical path; can consume parallel network capacity across many hosts.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously connected remote Agent Hosts for the account.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: `_authenticateAllConnections` launches one asynchronous reconciliation per connected host, so remote hosts refresh in parallel with no global limiter. Within a host/token, the WeakMap coalesces entitlement refreshes; host provider fan-out is parallel.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each connection owns its own `AgentHostAuthTokenCache`; unchanged entitlement metadata is suppressed independently per connection. Each remote host has an independent per-token discovery cache and refresh coalescer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for parallel per-connection scheduling and independent host requests; lower only for real-world host-count magnitude.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most users have few active remote hosts; there is no repository evidence of a realistically large connection count that would make the unbounded cross-host parallelism severe.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: fan-out is required to refresh independent host caches, per-host work is coalesced, and realistic connection cardinality is not shown to create a high-confidence regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: An entitlement-triggered background discovery refresh fails, followed by a model or utility request
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The failed refresh itself is background work, but clearing the cache moves the next `/copilot_internal/user` lookup onto the critical path of `models`, `responses`, `messages`, utility completion, restricted telemetry resolution, or another client lookup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retry `/copilot_internal/user` after the background refresh discarded the valid cached CAPI client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced retry per affected token/host after each failed entitlement refresh; if service remains unavailable, the user-facing operation waits and fails.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No entitlement-triggered failure could evict the valid entry; existing ordinary refresh failures retain an unexpired client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly blocks the next model/utility operation before its actual CAPI request can be issued.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The actual models/chat/utility CAPI request that can only start after client discovery resolves.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One intended operation per caller, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: With a valid cached client, these requests proceeded directly to their intended endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Its start is delayed by the newly forced discovery miss.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Failed entitlement refreshes across active token/host pairs; concurrent calls coalesce rather than multiplying requests.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One discovery retry is coalesced per token/host; all concurrent model callers wait behind that same promise. Different hosts/tokens retry independently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The refresh begins only from an unexpired cached client. The new non-401/403 failure branch clears `skuCell.value`; the next `_getEntryForToken` sees a miss. Concurrent next callers share `request.promise`, but the first must perform a new discovery. Ordinary cache-refresh failures already preserve an unexpired previous entry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the added cache clear, subsequent miss logic, HTTP fetch, and model-method awaits are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The added latency equals account-discovery network duration and depends on transient failure prevalence, but the extra blocking boundary is deterministic after the failure and can be especially visible while the endpoint remains degraded.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cache-lifecycle regression: a best-effort background failure converts an unexpired warm cache into a user-visible critical-path network miss.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial authentication or normal 30-minute discovery refresh emits account-discovery telemetry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial/ordinary discovery already gates the API operation that needs a client. Telemetry is emitted only after response processing. Any second entitlement revalidation from first authentication is not awaited by authentication after the initial discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing initial or cache-refresh GET to `/copilot_internal/user`; optionally one new background entitlement revalidation when the returned SKU still differs from the client hint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared initial/ordinary lookup per token; at most one coalesced entitlement lookup per token/request object.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Initial and normal TTL refresh network discovery already occurred, without entitlement revalidation or dedicated telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial/ordinary lookup behavior is pre-existing; entitlement lookup is background.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit fixed-shape telemetry containing outcome, timing, status, request ID, and account metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one event per actual HTTP discovery, including failures and superseded results; zero per model call or cache hit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous enqueue after discovery; no unbounded payload, collection walk, or repeated per-model emission.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Actual discovery attempts, normally one per token initially and at most once per refresh interval, plus rare entitlement revalidations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing `request.promise` coalesces ordinary discovery per token. Telemetry is one event per actual HTTP attempt. An ordinary refresh and entitlement refresh can overlap as two requests, but this requires an entitlement transition during the narrow refresh window and did not establish material impact.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Initial discovery remains one request on a cold per-token cache; warm entries older than the five-minute refresh buffer trigger one shared refresh. The new telemetry does not run on cache hits. On first authentication, a differing client hint can request one additional background revalidation after initial discovery; matching hints do not.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for event cardinality and cache behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Telemetry transport internals may batch asynchronously, but the event shape and frequency are tightly bounded in this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: telemetry allocation and transport cardinality are bounded to existing network attempts, and cache-hit/model-call fan-out is explicitly avoided.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 17 changed files and all diff hunks. Traced authentication events, local and remote connection fan-out, per-token discovery cache/coalescing, model-request critical paths, HTTP discovery, IPC, and telemetry emission. Submitted one medium-confidence-severity cache-lifecycle finding for evicting a valid client after failed background revalidation; no other changed mechanism met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
